term: Describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for Activity 4.2 (To construct an electromagnet and test paperclip lifting capacity.).
phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for activity 4.2 (to construct an electromagnet and test paperclip lifting capacity.).]
definition:
Aim: To construct an electromagnet and test paperclip lifting capacity.
Materials: Iron nail, Insulated copper wire (1m), 1.5V Cell, Switch, Paperclips
Steps: Wind copper wire tightly around iron nail. Connect coil ends to battery and switch. Turn switch ON and bring paperclips near nail head; turn switch OFF.
Observation: Clips stick to nail when current flows; clips drop immediately when circuit opens.
Principle: Soft iron exhibits temporary magnetism strictly while electric current flows.

phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: explain why nichrome wire is used in heating elements of electric irons, whereas copper wire is used for connecting leads.]

term: Describe an experiment to test electrical conduction in liquids using an LED circuit, and contrast tap water with distilled water.
phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: describe an experiment to test electrical conduction in liquids using an led circuit, and contrast tap water with distilled water.]
definition: 1. Setup: Connect a 3V battery cell in series with an LED and two open wire test leads. 2. Testing Distilled Water: Submerge leads into pure distilled water; the LED does not glow because distilled water lacks free mobile ions required to carry electric charge. 3. Testing Tap Water: Submerge leads into tap water; the LED glows dimly because dissolved mineral salts dissociate into mobile ions. 4. Conclusion: Liquids conduct electricity through mobile ion movement.
